questions.stem: Under section 106(1) of the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, who must develop procedures for dealing with emergencies?
options: The Minister of Transport
The harbour master
The authorized representative of the vessel
Every passenger on board
questions.explanation: Section 106(1) makes the authorized representative (usually the owner) responsible for developing procedures for safe operation and for emergencies and for ensuring that the crew and passengers receive safety training.

questions.stem: Which two duties does CSA s. 106(1) place on the authorized representative that relate to emergencies?
options: Hold a drill every week and keep the log for ten years
Develop emergency procedures and ensure crew and passengers receive safety training
Command the vessel in an emergency and sign the muster list
Report every drill to Transport Canada and have it approved
questions.explanation: Paragraphs 106(1)(b) and (c) require emergency procedures and safety training for crew and passengers. The frequency of drills and record-keeping come from other regulations, and the procedures are not submitted for approval.

questions.stem: What does SVR s. 420 require of the owner and operator of a passenger-carrying vessel?
options: That procedures be established for using life-saving appliances and fire extinguishing equipment in an emergency, and that the crew practise them to be proficient at all times
That drills be held weekly and recorded in an official log book
That a muster list be posted in every cabin
That all crew hold a master's certificate
questions.explanation: Section 420 requires procedures for using life-saving appliances and fire extinguishing equipment and requires the crew to practise them so as to be proficient at all times. It does not set a frequency.

questions.stem: A 9 m passenger-carrying vessel of 8 GT carries 10 passengers. Do the Fire and Boat Drills Regulations apply to her?
options: Yes, because any passenger vessel must follow the drill intervals
Yes, but only the weekly drill rule
No, but only because she is under 9 m
No: vessels of 15 GT or less that carry 12 or fewer passengers are excluded by s. 2(2)
questions.explanation: Section 2(2) of the FBDR excludes fishing vessels of 150 GT or less, cable ferries and vessels of 15 GT or less that carry 12 or fewer passengers. The vessel still has SVR s. 420.

questions.stem: A vessel certified to carry 30 passengers is making a voyage with passengers on the open coast. How often must fire and survival craft drills be held under the FBDR schedule?
options: At least once a week
At least once a month
At least once every two weeks
At least once a day
questions.explanation: A vessel other than a Safety Convention vessel that is certified for fewer than 50 passengers and carries passengers, on voyages other than sheltered waters, has a two-week interval. One week applies to Safety Convention vessels and vessels certified for 50 or more, and one month to cargo vessels.

questions.stem: A crew of 8 is about to sail. In the last month only 5 of them took part in a fire drill on board. What does the FBDR require?
options: Nothing, because 5 is a majority
A fire drill within 24 hours after embarking, because more than 25 per cent of the crew (3 of 8) did not take part
A fire drill within 7 days
A fire drill before the vessel sails, and no survival craft drill
questions.explanation: Section 20(2) requires a fire drill within 24 hours after embarking if more than 25 per cent of the crew did not take part in a fire drill on board in the previous month: 3 of 8 is 37.5 per cent. Section 20(3) applies the same rule to survival craft drills.

questions.stem: How often must each member of the crew take part in a fire drill and a survival craft drill under the FBDR?
options: At least once every month, one of each
At least once a year
Only when joining the vessel
At least once every three months
questions.explanation: Section 21 requires every crew member to take part in at least one fire drill and one survival craft drill every month.

questions.stem: Which statement is correct about running a drill with passengers on board?
options: The alarm is sounded without warning to test passengers' reactions
Passengers are not told so that the drill is realistic
Drills may not be held with passengers on board
Passengers are told beforehand that a drill will be held and there is no actual emergency, and the drill is carried out as if it were real
questions.explanation: Section 16 requires notification that a drill will be held and that there is no actual emergency before the signal is sounded, and s. 17 requires drills to be carried out as if there were an actual emergency as far as feasible.

questions.stem: After a drill, a fire hose was left on the deck and an extinguisher with a stiff pin was noticed. What do the Regulations require?
options: Leave the hose until the next drill and replace the extinguisher at the end of the season
Report the fault to Transport Canada before touching the extinguisher
Return equipment used to full operating condition immediately and remedy faults found as soon as practicable
Nothing, since it was only a drill
questions.explanation: Section 18 requires equipment used in a drill to be returned immediately to full operational condition and ready for reuse, and any faults found remedied as soon as practicable.

questions.stem: Which item must the master record for each drill under FBDR s. 37?
options: A list of the passengers' names
A detailed report of the drill and an evaluation of the competency and readiness of the entire crew
The cost of the equipment used
The master's weight and height
questions.explanation: Section 37 requires the date of each muster, detailed drill reports, a report of any drill not held or only partly held (with reasons), and an evaluation of the crew's competency and operational readiness. Records outside the official log book are kept on board for five years.

questions.stem: Drill records are kept in a deck log (not an official log book). For how long must they be kept on board?
options: Five years after the day of the last entry
One year
Until the next inspection
Ten years
questions.explanation: Section 37(3) requires a document that is not the official log book to be kept on board for five years after the last entry and made available to the Minister on request.

questions.stem: A vessel's master takes on a new deckhand. What do the Marine Personnel Regulations require before the deckhand begins duties?
options: Two weeks of watchkeeping before any training
A certificate in navigation
Nothing if the deckhand has fished before
On-board familiarization and safety training (TP 4957), with a record of the person, the equipment, the subject-matter and the dates
questions.explanation: Section 205(1) requires each person assigned a function to receive on-board familiarization and safety training in TP 4957 before starting any duty, and s. 206(2) requires the master to keep a record of each person trained, the equipment, the subject and the dates.

questions.stem: Does Transport Canada approve a small vessel's written safety procedures?
options: Yes, they must be approved before the vessel enters service
Yes, but only for passenger vessels
No, but an inspector may ask to see that they exist and are used
No, and inspectors may not ask to see them
questions.explanation: Transport Canada's template page says it does not require approval of the procedures, but an inspector may ask to see that they exist and are used.
